questions.prompt: Which tissue makes a plant grow in length?
questions.explain: Found at root and shoot tips.

questions.prompt: Which tissue carries water and minerals from the roots to the leaves?
questions.explain: Xylem vessels are hollow tubes carrying water upwards.

questions.prompt: The husk of a coconut is made of which tissue?
questions.explain: Dead cells with thick lignified walls: hard and stiff.

questions.prompt: Which tissue lets the leaf stalks and young stems bend without breaking?
questions.explain: Collenchyma cells are thickened at the corners, giving flexible support.
Meristems divide; simple permanent tissues have one cell type; complex tissues have several.

questions.prompt: Grass on a lawn grows back quickly after it is cut. Which tissue makes this possible?
options: Apical meristem at the cut tip
Intercalary meristem at the base of the leaves
questions.explain: Intercalary meristems at the nodes and leaf bases keep dividing after the tips are removed.

questions.prompt: How does phloem differ from xylem?
options: Phloem carries food in both directions and is mostly living
Phloem carries water upwards and is dead
Phloem is found only in roots
questions.explain: Xylem: water up, mostly dead cells. Phloem: food up and down, living cells.

questions.prompt: Explain how the structure of xylem vessels suits their function.
questions.modelAnswer: Xylem vessels are long, hollow tubes made of dead cells joined end to end with no cytoplasm or end walls, so water can flow freely up the plant. Their walls are thickened with lignin, which makes them strong enough to support the plant and stop the tubes collapsing.
rubric: Hollow tubes with no end walls or cytoplasm
Lignin makes them strong and supportive
